hero.title: Triratna: Three Jewels of Jainism
hero.description: The ethical and philosophical foundation of Jainism designed to attain liberation (Moksha) from the cycle of rebirth.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: Evolution of Jain doctrine from oral tradition to canonical scriptures.

cards.details: Life of Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara, who formalized the Triratna framework.
First Jain Council at Pataliputra; attempt to codify the Angas and maintain the Three Jewels.

mnemonics.title: Mnemonics & Tricks to Remember
mnemonics.description: Use the acronym K.F.C. (Jain style) for the Three Jewels.

items.title: K.F.C.
items.decryption: Samyak Gyana (Knowledge), Samyak Darshana (Faith), Samyak Charitra (Conduct). Remember it as the 'spiritual sustenance' for the soul.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Confusing Jain Triratna (Knowledge/Faith/Conduct) with Buddhist Triratna (Buddha/Dhamma/Sangha).
Assuming 'Ahimsa' is a separate fourth jewel; it is technically a subset of 'Conduct' (Charitra).

deepDive.description: Master the key concepts and dimensions of this topic.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Essence

  • Samyak Darshana: Right Faith
  • Samyak Gyana: Right Knowledge
  • Samyak Charitra: Right Conduct

Goal

  • Attaining Kevala Gyana (Omniscience)
  • Cessation of Karma (Nirjara)
  • Final Moksha
  • Right Faith (Samyak Darshana): Belief in the teachings of Tirthankaras and the nature of reality.
  • Right Knowledge (Samyak Gyana): Correct understanding of the soul (Jiva) and matter (Ajiva).
  • Right Conduct (Samyak Charitra): Practice of non-violence (Ahimsa), truth (Satya), non-stealing (Asteya), celibacy (Brahmacharya), and non-possession (Aparigraha).
JewelSanskrit TermCore Significance
FaithSamyak DarshanaFoundational belief in Jain doctrines.
KnowledgeSamyak GyanaIntellectual grasp of the karmic cycle.
ConductSamyak CharitraApplication of ethics in daily life.
